title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 5)
summary: NH reads passages of the Hagakure on the levels of mastery, defeating oneself, preparing for critical matters in advance, and knowledge versus the Way, and applies them to lifting. His themes are that there are no limits, that you should train against yourself, that knowledge without practice is worthless, and that body and mind must be trained together for life.
claims: Everyone has to pass through the levels of skill; gifted people move through them faster (novice for four weeks, intermediate for six months) but cannot skip them
An intermediate is defined not by strength or size but by knowing what they want and being able to name their weak points
People at the middle level often use their new eye for flaws to put beginners down; only point out flaws to help
Being proud of what you have earned is good; humility means knowing you are excellent and can still improve, not humiliating yourself
When he sees a beginner in the gym he does not feel superior; he sees someone ten years behind who could reach his level
True experts don't need to announce what they know; it shows
There is no natural limit and no maintaining; you keep progressing until you die
Perfection exists only in God; humans stay imperfect, so the master stays aware of his flaws and never becomes content
In a fight and in training you are really trying to defeat yourself, not the opponent
Training to surpass others leads to stagnation once no one is left to beat; training to surpass yourself never dies
Tiny daily improvements compound into a huge difference over a year
Prepare for big, foreseeable crises well in advance so you can deal with them in seconds when they arrive
People who read an abstract and think they are experts are worse than ordinary people, because they lack knowledge and are also conceited
You must wield both the pen and the sword; the body and the spirit grow together and neither is enough alone
Knowing the Way means discovering your own faults through endless introspection and training body and mind for your whole life
Using science to place yourself above others and criticise them makes it worthless; it should be positive
